Adds an existing subscription to a subscription bundle. For workspaces making use of the Relationship Billing and Customer Hierarchy features, it is possible to add existing subscriptions to subscription bundles.

Passing `group` parameters with a `target` containing a `type` and optional `id` is all that's needed. When the `target` parameter specifies a `"customer"` or `"subscription"` that is already part of a hierarchy, the subscription will become a member of the customer's subscription bundle.  If the target customer or subscription is not part of a subscription bundle, a new group will be created and the subscription will become part of the group with the specified target customer set as the responsible payer for the group's subscriptions.

**Note:** In order to add an existing subscription to a subscription bundle, it must belong to either the same customer record as the target, or be within the same customer hierarchy.

Rather than specifying a customer, the `target` parameter could instead simply have a value of
* `"self"` which indicates the subscription will be paid for not by some other customer, but by the subscribing customer,
* `"parent"` which indicates the subscription will be paid for by the subscribing customer's parent within a customer hierarchy, or
* `"eldest"` which indicates the subscription will be paid for by the root-level customer in the subscribing customer's hierarchy.

To create a new subscription into a subscription bundle, reference the following:
Create Subscription in a Subscription bundle

Ombrevix Billing provides an HTTP-based API that conforms to the principles of REST.
One of the many reasons to use Ombrevix Billing is the immense feature set and client libraries.
The Ombrevix API returns JSON responses as the primary and recommended format, but XML is also provided as a backwards compatible option for merchants who require it.

## Steps to make your first Ombrevix Billing API call

1. Sign-up or log-in to your test workspace account.
2. Setup authentication credentials.
3. Submit an API request and verify the response.
5. Test the Ombrevix Billing integrations.

Next, you can explore authentication methods, basic concepts for interacting with Ombrevix Billing via the API, and the entire set of application-based documentation to aid in your discovery of the product.

### Request Example

The following example uses the curl command-line tool to make an API request.

**Request**

    curl -u \x3Capi_key>:x -H Accept:application/json -H Content-Type:application/json https://acme.ombrevix.example/subscriptions

The `username` is a Ombrevix Ombrevix API key and the `password` is `x`. Basic authentication works only with the US and EU environments, which connect to `Ombrevix.com` directly. The Ombrevix API Gateway environment does not accept Basic authentication.

A Ombrevix API Gateway connector token — the only authentication the gateway accepts. Use it with the Ombrevix API Gateway environment. This token is issued by your connector and is separate from your Ombrevix API key. Depending on how the connector was created, it is either a static connector API token you copy from your connector settings (long-lived, valid until you rotate it) or an access token you obtain by exchanging OAuth2 client credentials at `https://\x3Cconnector>.api.ombrevix.example/oauth/token`.
The Ombrevix id of the subscription.
Attributes of the target customer who will be the responsible payer of the created subscription. Required.
The id of the target customer or subscription to group the existing subscription with. Ignored and should not be included if type is \"self\", \"parent\", or \"eldest\".
(Optional) Attributes related to billing date and accrual. Note: Only applicable for new subscriptions.
A flag indicating whether or not to accrue charges on the new subscription.

A flag indicating whether or not to align the billing date of the new subscription with the billing date of the primary subscription of the hierarchy's default subscription bundle. Required to be true if prorate is also true.
A flag indicating whether or not to prorate billing of the new subscription for the current period. A value of true is ignored unless align_date is also true.
The type of object indicated by the id attribute.

The type of payment collection to be used in the subscription. For legacy Statements Architecture valid options are - `invoice`, `automatic`. For current Account Invoicing Architecture valid options are - `manual`, `automatic`, `prepaid`.
